comment.comment:
been digging into $WORM / Agent Wormhole and there’s a pretty interesting thesis forming here.

the easiest way to understand it:

AI agents are slowly evolving from “tools that answer questions” into software that can actually control and move real money.

and robinhood is heading directly in that direction.

they’ve launched agentic trading infrastructure that allows AI agents to connect through MCP, analyze markets and execute trades.

vlad has been pretty clear about where he thinks this is going:

“Our mission has always been to democratize finance for all, and now, that mission extends to AI agents.”

but once you give autonomous agents access to money, you create a completely new problem:

who makes sure the agent doesn’t fuck up?

an agent can misunderstand an instruction.

interact with something malicious.

send the wrong token.

use the wrong chain.

sign something it shouldn’t.

this is where Agent Wormhole comes in.

instead of building another trading agent, they’re building security infrastructure around them.

their x402 Guard is designed to verify things like the recipient, amount, token and chain BEFORE an agent signs a transaction.

and that’s what caught my attention:

robinhood is building infrastructure that gives AI agents financial power.

Agent Wormhole is building infrastructure designed to make those financial actions safer.

and now vlad has liked their content again.

obviously, a like isn’t a partnership or endorsement.

but the direction robinhood is publicly moving toward is almost exactly the future $WORM is positioning itself for.

AI agents managing real money will need security.

the more money agents control, the more valuable that security layer could become.

still early and the team needs to execute, but this is exactly the kind of robinhood eco play i like researching:

not another random meme.

an actual product sitting in front of a potentially massive trend.
